title: Gulf states tell citizens to leave Lebanon after Meqdad clan kidnappings
why: Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar issued the warning on 15 August 2012, and reports add Kuwait. It followed the Meqdad clan's announcement that it had seized more than 20 Syrians, a Turkish national and a Saudi in reprisal for the abduction in Syria of a clan member.
dup_of: Saudi Arabia, Qatar and UAE urge citizens to leave Lebanon after kidnappings

title: Lebanon ends visa-free entry for Syrians
why: From 5 January 2015 Syrians needed to show a reason for entry under set categories, ending decades of free movement at the border. About 1.1 million Syrians were UNHCR-registered in Lebanon at the time.

title: Rebels take the Nasib crossing, cutting the Syria-Jordan road used by Lebanese exports
why: An offensive that began on 1 April 2015 pushed government forces out of Nasib, the last official crossing between Syria and Jordan. It had carried goods from Lebanon and Turkey to Gulf markets, and it stayed closed until October 2018.

title: UNHCR suspends registration of Syrians in Lebanon at the government's request
why: Registration was halted from 5 May 2015 until further notice. Social Affairs Minister Rashid Derbas said Lebanon had reached capacity, with about 1.2 million Syrians, and told Al Jazeera that the glass cannot fit one more drop. UNHCR counts in the Hub fall after this date.
dup_of: Foreign Ministry tells UNHCR to stop registering Syrian refugees

title: Saudi Arabia cancels military aid to Lebanon over Hezbollah and Iran
why: Announced on 19 February 2016: the $3 billion programme for French arms for the Lebanese army, and a further $1 billion for security services in some reports. Riyadh cited Lebanon's stance toward Iran after the January attack on its embassy in Tehran. The UAE and Bahrain backed the decision.
dup_of: Saudi Arabia halts $3 billion package to the Lebanese army

title: Hariri resigns on Saudi television and returns to Beirut weeks later
why: Saad Hariri announced his resignation from Riyadh on 4 November 2017, citing fear of assassination and Iranian interference. He returned to Beirut on 21 November and on 22 November suspended the resignation at President Aoun's request.

title: Jordan and Syria reopen the Nasib-Jaber crossing after three years
why: The crossing opened to civilians and trade on 15 October 2018 after Syrian forces retook the area in July. President Aoun said it would revive Lebanese productive sectors and lower export costs to Arab markets.

title: US Caesar Act sanctions on Syria take effect
why: Signed in December 2019, the act came into force on 17 June 2020. It targets those who knowingly support the Syrian government in oil and gas, military, aviation and construction. Lebanese banks and traders braced for exposure because Syria's foreign payments often ran through neighbouring banks. It shaped the 2021-22 gas plan, because US officials had to confirm that Egyptian gas through Syria was not sanctionable (see the 21 June 2022 row). It was repealed on 18 December 2025.

title: Saudi Arabia bans Lebanese produce after a captagon seizure in pomegranates
why: Jeddah customs reported more than 5.3 million captagon pills hidden in a pomegranate shipment from Lebanon, and Riyadh announced the ban on 23 April 2021, in force from 25 April. It covered produce from or transiting Lebanon until Beirut gave guarantees on smuggling. Reported fruit and vegetable exports to Saudi Arabia were up to $24 million a year.

title: Iraq and Lebanon sign a fuel oil deal paid in goods and services
why: Caretaker Energy Minister Raymond Ghajar and Iraq's Finance Minister Ali Allawi signed in Baghdad on 24 July 2021: one million tonnes of heavy fuel oil over a year for Electricite du Liban, in exchange for goods and services, mainly medical care. A Legal Agenda study describes the oil as being swapped for compatible products through monthly tenders.

title: Egypt, Jordan, Syria and Lebanon agree a road map for gas and power to Lebanon
why: Energy ministers met in Amman and agreed to send Egyptian gas through Jordan and Syria on the Arab Gas Pipeline to northern Lebanon, and Jordanian electricity through Syria at a later stage. No timeline was given. The US had backed the idea in August through its ambassador in Beirut.

title: Saudi Arabia expels the Lebanese ambassador and halts all imports from Lebanon
why: The step followed Information Minister George Kordahi's remarks, taped before his appointment, calling the Houthis defenders and the Yemen war pointless. Riyadh recalled its own ambassador, gave Lebanon's ambassador 48 hours to leave and stopped all imports on 29 October 2021. Prime Minister Mikati said he regretted the decision.
dup_of: Saudi Arabia expels Lebanese ambassador over Kordahi remarks

title: Kuwait, the UAE and Bahrain follow Saudi Arabia in recalling ambassadors
why: Kuwait recalled its ambassador and gave Lebanon's ambassador 48 hours to leave. The UAE withdrew its diplomats and barred its citizens from travelling to Lebanon. Bahrain gave Lebanon's ambassador 48 hours that night. Kordahi resigned in December (see the existing row).

title: Lebanon, Syria and Egypt sign the Egyptian gas import deal
why: Officials signed a contract for 22.95 billion cubic feet a year of Egyptian gas via Jordan and Syria, enough for about 450 MW or four more hours of power a day. World Bank financing depended on power-sector reforms, and US officials said they could confirm the project was not sanctionable only after the terms were disclosed. See the 29 December 2025 row for the later Lebanon-Egypt memorandum.

title: Arab League lets Syria resume participation, with a liaison committee including Lebanon
why: Foreign ministers meeting in Cairo on 7 May 2023 ended Syria's suspension, which began in November 2011. The decision named refugees and drug smuggling as issues to resolve and set up a follow-up committee that includes Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Iraq and Lebanon.

title: Hezbollah opens a second front a day after the Hamas attack
why: From 8 October 2023 Hezbollah fired guided rockets and shells at Israeli positions in the Shebaa Farms, which it said was in solidarity with Gaza, and Israel answered with drones and artillery. It was the largest escalation on the border since 2006.
dup_of: Hezbollah opens a front against Israel

title: Assad government falls in Syria
why: Opposition forces led by Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham took Damascus on 8 December 2024 and Assad fled to Russia. Crowds celebrated in Bar Elias. Clashes between Syria's new authorities and Hezbollah followed along the border, and UNHCR later reported about 378,000 Syrians returning from Lebanon (see the December 2025 row).

title: Lebanon and Syria sign a border demarcation and security deal in Jeddah
why: Defence Ministers Michel Menassa and Murhaf Abu Qasra signed it under Saudi hosting on 28 March 2025, creating legal and specialised committees for demarcation. It followed two days of border clashes on 16 and 17 March that killed 10, ended by a ceasefire between the same ministers.

title: US and Israel strike Iran and kill Khamenei
why: The strikes on 28 February 2026 killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and targeted missile, air defence and nuclear sites. Hezbollah, Iran's closest ally in Lebanon, joined two days later.

title: Hezbollah fires on Israel after the strikes on Iran; the 2026 Lebanon war begins
why: On 2 March 2026 Hezbollah launched strikes on Israel, which it called a response to the attack on Iran, and Israel hit Hezbollah targets across Lebanon. The cabinet banned Hezbollah's military activity the same day (see the existing row).
